title: D-Link warns of multiple zero-days in DGS-3130 Series switches
content_md: D-Link shared mitigation measures for multiple unpatched security flaws affecting DGS-3130 series managed Gigabit stackable switches. These switch models provide multi-gigabit uplinks, allowing enterprise network administrators to eliminate data bottlenecks, and are designed primarily for small-to-medium businesses (SMBs) and metro Ethernet deployments. While D-Link didn't share details on these flaws and has yet to publicly disclose the CVE IDs for easier tracking, it said Spectrum Community Solutions network engineer Giresh Kumar Enugu found the bugs in the D-Link Discovery Protocol (DDP) authentication, access control, and information handling. Successful exploitation could allow attackers to obtain sensitive device data, make unauthorized credential/configuration changes, leak SNMP communities, or cause service disruptions and device resets. The zero-days affect multiple DGS-3130-30TS firmware versions, and the company is still investigating the impact on other D-Link switching platforms and firmware security mechanisms (including SSH service security configuration, safeguards underlying operating-system credentials, and handles firmware encryption/embedded cryptographic keys). "The reported vulnerabilities involve the D-Link Discovery Protocol (DDP) and certain components of the device's firmware security architecture," D-Link said .
